name: Demodocus
bio: Demodocus is one of the named epigrammatists whose short poems are preserved in the Greek Anthology. Paton's Index of Authors dates the poet to the 5th century BC.
This archive carries the 4 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the fourth volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Loeb, 1918): Book XI: 235, 236, 237, 238.

poems.title: Book XI, 235
poems.author: Demodocus
poems.text: This, too, is by Demodocus : “ The Chians are bad, not one bad and another not, but all bad except Procles, and Procles is a Chian.”

poems.title: Book XI, 236
poems.author: Demodocus
poems.text: All Cilicians are bad men, but among the Cilicians the only good man is Cinyras, and Cinyras is a Cilician.

poems.title: Book XI, 237
poems.author: Demodocus
poems.text: An evil viper once bit a Cappadocian, but it died itself, having tasted the venomous blood.

poems.title: Book XI, 238
poems.author: Demodocus
poems.text: The Cappadocians are always bad, but when they get a belt they are worse, and for the sake of gain they are the worst of all, and if once or twice they get hold of a large carriage they are as bad as bad can be for a year. I implore thee, O King, let it not be four times, lest the whole world slide to ruin, becoming cappadocianified. ' The women of Lemnos, who had killed their husbands, were afflicted by Venus with an evil odour.

poems.title: Cinyras the Cilician (Mackail)
poems.author: Demodocus
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: All Cilicians are bad men; among the Cilicians there is one good man, Cinyras, and Cinyras is a Cilician.
